title: WatchLog incident candidate
description: Structured output a model emits when it proposes an incident. The APPLICATION decides whether this becomes a real operations incident; the model only proposes. Validated server-side; malformed payloads are rejected (never rendered).

incident_definition_id.description: Must reference an existing definition id under incidents/ (e.g. security.after_hours_restricted_area). The model may not invent incident types.

camera_ids.description: Only cameras in the authorized scope for this request.

coverage.description: Coverage class over the window (from wl_site_coverage_report_classes). UNVERIFIED forces tier DETECTION_GAP.

drivers.description: The specific evidence that produced this candidate. Empty drivers => not allowed (cannot be STRONG).

ref.description: An authorized event_id / snapshot ref / observation id — never a fabricated reference.

observation_id.description: Optional: a taxonomy/observations primitive id, e.g. PERSON_PRESENT.

summary.description: Truthful, evidence-scoped language (see core/truth.md). Must NOT over-escalate: 'Person observed in restricted area after hours', not 'Intruder breaking in', unless evidence supports it.

uncertainty.description: What is NOT established (required when tier != STRONG).

recommended_actions.description: Human-facing next steps only. Any device action goes through action.schema.json + the Site Control gate, never here.
